title: Enhanced Omni-Channel routing
summary: Explain how queued service work becomes eligible for a person based on presence, capacity, and routing configuration, with a complete no-license simulation path.
prerequisites: M01 access requirements and M30 observable outcomes.
learningObjectives: Distinguish ownership assignment from active work routing.
Evaluate presence and capacity using a concrete trace.
Separate a simulated clinic from an optional live product lab.

sections.heading: Understand the mechanism
body: A Case records a customer's service issue. A queue groups work that a team can handle. An assignment rule can place a Case with an owner or queue, but that is not the same as deciding which available employee should receive the next item. Omni-Channel adds routing behavior based on configured eligibility, workload, priority, and, when used, skills.

Presence describes whether a person is available for the relevant work. Capacity describes how much work the configuration allows them to handle. A work item consumes capacity according to the chosen model. Queue membership alone does not prove that a person is currently eligible: they may be offline, at capacity, missing a needed skill, or unavailable for the relevant service channel.

Use current Enhanced Omni-Channel documentation rather than building a new learning path around retired Standard Omni-Channel instructions. The product and its available channels depend on edition, licenses, and org configuration. This clinic's mandatory path is the supplied routing simulation. A live setup is optional in a suitably entitled training org and must not be required to complete the core Middle project.

Omni-Channel and OmniStudio are different things. Omni-Channel routes service work; OmniStudio provides tools for guided interactions and related integration/data experiences. Similar names do not make them interchangeable. The useful interview answer explains the business operation and the configured routing stages rather than listing both products together.

callouts.text: Being a queue member is only one condition; presence, capacity, and the routing policy determine current eligibility.

sections.heading: Northstar Motors worked example
body: Use this simplified capacity model: each employee has capacity 4 and each Case costs 2 units. Anna is online with 2 units used; Max is online with all 4 used; Oleg is offline with 0 used. All three belong to the support queue. Only Anna is eligible for the next item. After accepting it, she reaches 4 and a second item must wait unless someone else's eligibility changes.

Now Max completes work and drops to 2 used units. He becomes eligible under the simple queue scenario. Add a required EV-service skill that only Anna has: Max's free capacity is no longer sufficient to qualify him. These examples intentionally avoid a tie between equally eligible employees, so they do not invent the product's tie-breaking algorithm.

callouts.text: Why is Oleg ineligible even though his capacity usage is zero?

sections.heading: Build and inspect
body: Mandatory: work through the provided trace and explain decisions. Optional live lab: verify Enhanced Omni-Channel entitlement, use synthetic Cases, and record the actual capacity model and configuration; do not assume it matches the simplified simulation.

steps.title: Trace eligibility
steps.instruction: For each person, evaluate queue membership, presence, available capacity, and any required skill. Record the first failed condition.
steps.expected: Every routing decision has a concrete explanation.

steps.title: Change one condition
steps.instruction: Simulate Max completing work, Anna going offline, and an EV skill requirement. Predict each result before changing the trace.
steps.expected: Capacity and skill are not confused with one another.

steps.title: Optional live verification
steps.instruction: In an entitled training org, configure a Case service channel, routing configuration, queue membership, presence settings, and the appropriate console utility. Test one online worker and one ineligible worker.
steps.expected: Evidence names the actual configuration and distinguishes it from simulation.

sections.heading: Failure cases and boundaries
body: A Case sitting in a queue is not proof that routing is broken. Check the service channel, eligible presence, capacity, membership, and routing configuration before changing ownership arbitrarily.

Closing a browser or changing a record status may interact with the configured capacity model differently than assumed. Verify the actual model instead of transferring simulation rules without inspection.

callouts.text: No paid license or trial is required for the mandatory clinic; mark live product steps Not run when unavailable.

exercise.title: Explain a routing decision
exercise.brief: Submit the provided simulation with three condition changes and an optional separately labeled live observation.
steps: Compare assignment ownership with active routing.
acceptance: Every chosen or excluded person has a reason.
No unsupported tie-breaking rule is invented.
Simulation and live evidence are clearly separated.
exercise.stretch: Explain one limitation and propose a small follow-up experiment before extending the implementation.

knowledgeCheck.question: Why is a queue not enough?
knowledgeCheck.answer: Membership identifies a team, but current presence, capacity, and routing requirements still determine eligibility.

knowledgeCheck.question: How does an assignment rule differ?
knowledgeCheck.answer: It assigns ownership; Omni-Channel handles configured distribution of eligible work to available recipients.

knowledgeCheck.question: Is OmniStudio the routing engine?
knowledgeCheck.answer: No. It is a different product family with different purposes.

recap: Keep product entitlement optional for the core course.
